ai.description: This small frog reaches 25–30 mm. It is yellowish-brown with dark dorsal markings and a distinct dark lateral stripe. Key features include large, adhesive toe pads and a pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Chirixalus nongkhorensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark brown triangular or Y-shaped marking on its back, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Chirixalus nongkhorensis* typically inhabits lowland evergreen forests, scrublands, and agricultural areas, often breeding in temporary pools within bamboo thickets.
ai.behavior: The Nongkhor Asian Treefrog is strictly nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for small insects among the vegetation surrounding forest pools and marshes.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Chirixalus nongkhorensis* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 50–150 eggs in foam nests attached to vegetation overhanging temporary water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Chirixalus nongkhorensis* is found in Northeast India, specifically in Assam and Meghalaya, typically inhabiting low-to-mid elevation forest habitats.
ai.callDescription: The Nongkhor Asian Treefrog produces a series of short, high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard while calling from vegetation near stagnant forest pools.
